correctness.rationale: For each triple with sorted internal transformed edge weights a≤b≤c, its three thresholds are b,c,c, yielding conditional probability (1-b)^(n-3)(1-c)^(2n-6); integration gives exact expectation. Distinct closed triples cannot intersect. For fixed disjoint families the cross-family edge-factor tends to 1 under n-scaling and an integrable e^[-(b+2c)/2] majorant establishes joint factorial-moment measures. The total intensity equals 1/18 and the finite checker exhaustively reproduces n=4. Limits are proven analytically, not inferred from experiments.

originality.rationale: Cooper–Frieze (1995, full text sections on model and isolated cycles) counts connected isolated 2-nearest-neighbor components, rather than closed directed 3-sinks with possible incoming edges. Its isolated-triangle limit 0.00415239 is incompatible with, and does not entail, the new 1/18 count and three-weight intensity. Ball (2014) uses geometric dependent distances and logarithmically growing k. Published reciprocal one-neighbor pair formula and independent k-out directed cycle results have different neighbor-selection dependence/outdegree. Multiple published-finding corpus and literature queries found no direct stronger coverage. A general marked Poisson theorem could recover the limit but no such applicable result with the explicit intensity was identified.
residual_risks: An unlocated general rare-motif theorem might imply part of the Poisson convergence, though no explicit same marked measure was found.
The 1995 source is a dated manuscript and journal article; its earliest public exact calendar day was not verified. The selected archival first-public day is verified from the 2014 arXiv version.

value.rationale: The smallest absorbing strongly connected motif in a directed two-neighbor network is a complete bidirected triangle. Counting those cores without disallowing incoming arrows measures directed local trapping, rather than undirected graph disconnection. Its exact finite-size mean, nondegenerate Poisson count and joint three-edge weight intensity allow multi-threshold estimates for reciprocal-cluster strength; the older isolated-component frequency does not determine this quantity.
